findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, unreadable path).
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, IOError> or an equivalent typed domain error; propagate fs::read_to_string failures with map_err or ?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or missing second field.
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line aborts the entire batch load instead of skipping or returning a per-record parse error
findings.fix: use .map_err() or ? to propagate ParseIntError; if batch tolerance is needed, return Result per record and filter/collect with ok()

findings.problem: lossy as u16 conversion after parse: values in 65536..u32::MAX silently truncate to u16 range.
findings.failure_mode: out-of-range values wrap silently, producing incorrect domain data without any signal to the caller
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap_or_else(|_| u32::MAX)) or parse directly to u16 via parts[1].parse::<u16>() with proper error propagation; reject values > u16::MAX

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked indexing on a Vec with no bounds check. If a line has fewer than 2 comma-separated fields, this panics with index-out-of-bounds.
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV (short line) causes panic instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use get(0) and get(1) with ok_or or map_err, or use split_once(',') to destructure exactly two fields without allocation

findings.problem: println!("loaded ...") is a side-effecting I/O call inside a library function that is supposed to be a data-loading action. This couples the core loading logic to stdout logging.
findings.failure_mode: library consumers cannot suppress audit logs; stdout pollution makes downstream consumers break; logging is mixed into data-loading logic instead of being pushed to the imperative shell
findings.fix: remove println! from the library function; return a count or per-record metadata if the caller needs to log; push logging to the shell layer that calls load_audits

findings.problem: Collecting all split parts into Vec<String> then indexing is wasteful: allocates a Vec, clones every trimmed string, then discards all but the first two. For a 2-field line this is unnecessary heap allocation.
findings.failure_mode: increased memory pressure and allocation latency on every line; not a correctness bug but violates bounded-allocation discipline for simple parsing
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get two &str parts, then trim and clone only the needed fields; avoids Vec allocation entirely

findings.problem: load_audits mixes file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, validation, and logging (println) in a single function. The functional core (parsing/validating a line into a Record) is not separated from the imperative shell (reading the file, printing).
findings.failure_mode: the parsing logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation without mocking filesystem access; testability and correctness are degraded
findings.fix: extract a pure fn parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> and have load_audits call it after reading the file; push println! to the caller/shell

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for this I/O-bound loading path. The function allocates a Vec<String> per line and clones into String fields — if this is on a hot path, there is no measured baseline.
findings.failure_mode: performance regression risk: unmeasured allocations could become a bottleneck under load with no alert
findings.fix: add a criterion or divan benchmark for load_audits with a realistic input file; measure allocations and throughput; add a baseline to Cargo.toml bench section

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_audits throughput or allocation profile
no profiler evidence for hot-path characterization of the I/O + parse loop
no allocation audit (e.g., heaptrack, valgrind, or criterion allocation tracking) for the Vec<String> per-line pattern
no command-layer or CLI entry point evidence — the imperative shell that calls load_audits is not present in this crate
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. The crate compiles as a minimal eval fixture. Four BLOCKERs (unwrap on I/O, unwrap on parse, lossy as-conversion, unchecked indexing) will cause panics or silent data corruption on malformed input. The functional core is not separated from I/O, preventing isolated testing. Benchmark and profiler evidence is entirely absent.
